tricks.name: Public leaderboard probe thresholding
tricks.summary: Tune post-processing thresholds against public leaderboard feedback when local validation is too weak or distribution-shifted.
applies_when: A competition exposes repeated public leaderboard feedback and the objective is a thresholded or discretized metric.
The architect has already selected a valid base CDG and needs to catalog leaderboard-specific tactical risk.
do_not_use_when: The target setting has no public feedback loop or prohibits leaderboard probing.
A held-out validation split is reliable enough to tune thresholds without public feedback.
validation_requirements: Record a local validation score before and after the threshold change.
Document the number of public feedback probes and show the tactic is not being encoded as base CDG structure.
tricks.architect_hint: Mention only as a high-risk post-processing tactic for novel or under-covered cases; never use it to choose the base CDG.

audit.notes: Cataloged for architect awareness because public-feedback tuning can explain some solution writeups but should not become CDG topology.

tricks.name: Hidden group leakage diagnostic
tricks.summary: Look for repeated users, devices, sessions, files, or collection batches whose membership can leak target information across nominal train/test boundaries.
applies_when: Rows share opaque IDs, timestamps, batches, files, cameras, devices, or locations that may define hidden groups.
The base CDG is tabular, image, sensor, or multimodal and missing techniques mention magic groups, counts, folds, or leakage diagnostics.
do_not_use_when: The benchmark contract explicitly forbids exploiting non-causal group artifacts.
Group structure is already represented as a standard validation constraint or feature-engineering stage.
validation_requirements: Confirm the group signal on a leakage-safe split.
Document whether the tactic is a diagnostic, a validation split constraint, or an allowed feature.
tricks.architect_hint: Surface as a leakage-risk diagnostic and validation constraint before suggesting any feature that uses hidden groups.

audit.notes: Kept as a trick because it may be an invalid leak, a valid split rule, or a legitimate feature depending on benchmark policy.

tricks.name: Metric-bound target clipping
tricks.summary: Clip predictions or transformed targets to known metric bounds, physical ranges, or submission limits after model inference.
applies_when: The metric or benchmark rules define valid numeric ranges.
Training targets have outliers that destabilize MAE, RMSLE, R2, or ranking-sensitive metrics.
do_not_use_when: The clipping range is inferred from public test feedback rather than a domain or metric constraint.
The base CDG already models clipping as a normal metric post-processing stage.
validation_requirements: Show clipping improves or preserves held-out validation.
Record the source of bounds: metric, physics, business rule, or training-label support.
tricks.architect_hint: Treat as optional metric post-processing for a selected CDG, not as a reason to create a new CDG.

audit.notes: This is often legitimate, but it should remain a tactic because the valid bounds are benchmark-specific.

tricks.name: Test-distribution pseudo-labeling
tricks.summary: Use confident predictions on public or unlabeled test-distribution data as additional training signal after validating that the feedback loop is stable.
applies_when: Unlabeled target-domain examples are available and distribution shift is a major source of error.
The selected CDG already has a training loop that can ingest extra labeled or weakly labeled examples.
do_not_use_when: Pseudo-labels are derived from prohibited private labels or leaderboard probes.
The first-stage model has weak precision and would amplify errors.
validation_requirements: Use out-of-fold or held-out validation to set confidence thresholds.
Track performance before and after pseudo-labeling and inspect class-balance drift.
tricks.architect_hint: Present as a validation-gated training tactic for domain adaptation, especially in image, text, and tabular competitions.

audit.notes: Pseudo-labeling is reusable, but test-distribution use and confidence policy are benchmark-specific enough to catalog here.

tricks.name: Inference-budget brute-force search
tricks.summary: Spend unusually large inference or submission-time compute on repeated sampling, local repair, solver retries, or exhaustive candidate search.
applies_when: The benchmark permits heavyweight offline inference, repeated sampling, solver loops, or local search.
The selected CDG is planning, search, LLM tool use, or constrained optimization and candidate quality improves with more attempts.
do_not_use_when: Strict latency, cost, or real-time constraints are part of the target setting.
The tactic exploits an execution environment quirk rather than a permitted search budget.
validation_requirements: Report compute budget, number of samples or retries, and marginal return curves.
Confirm generated candidates remain valid under the benchmark constraints.
tricks.architect_hint: Offer as a costed inference tactic after a planning/search or LLM tool-use CDG is selected.

audit.notes: Cataloged as a tactic because it changes compute allocation rather than the core CDG topology.
